_note: Round 56 (more findable pages, owner: "use what we have and show it in a new manner ... split numbers that are together"): the generated page families, written by seo_pages.mjs with seo_families.mjs from the map's own numbers, in every site language. parts: one page per part of the panel (key) with its address (slug) and side (ua: support for Ukraine; back: money flowing back from it; rus: what Russia kept from trade; frozen: the return Russia lost on frozen money; cost: outside the totals). A part gets a page only where at least minCountries countries have it and the amounts add up to at least minTotal (EUR bn, by size), and not when a topic page of seo_topics.json already ranks it (rank: part:<key>). Its name in each language is in seo_i18n.mjs (PART). years: the years with a page of support for Ukraine (/ukraine-aid-<year>/) and of trade with Russia (/trade-with-russia-<year>/); the last year runs to the data's last month. compare: pairs of countries (ISO codes, in the order searched) with a page /compare/<a>-vs-<b>/, from the keyword research of 26 October 2026; pairwiseTop: the largest donors to Ukraine in euros, every pair of them compared too (the larger donor first).

country._note: Round 57: the rule of round 56 that gives an English country page the title "Does ... trade with Russia?" (seo_templates.mjs): where its trade with Russia is searched at least minTrade times (pipeline/seo_demand.json), at least ratio times more than its aid or help, and its aid is searched fewer than maxAid times (the countries whose aid is much searched keep the aid question). It replaces the list of ten countries with hand-written titles.

phrasing._note: Round 59 (owner approved: "titles in the words people search"): the country page's title, heading and questions in the phrasing people search in the page's language, from Google's monthly volumes of the keyword discovery of 27 October 2026 (seo_demand.json ask: per country and language, given = what it gave Ukraine, support / helping = the question about Russia, trade = its trade with Russia). The question about what it gave is the title where its support for Ukraine is very likely and that phrasing is searched at least minDemand times a month and at least as often as the question about Russia; the question about Russia (support or helping, whichever is searched more) where that phrasing itself is searched at least minDemand times and the two together at least as often as the other; round 59b: no default verb, so a country page asks "Does ... support Russia?" only where people search for it. Its trade section's heading and question name the pair (India–Russia trade) where its trade is searched at least minTrade times. The questions' scores (seo_country.mjs) add these volumes. Otherwise the chance level's own title.

relations._note: Round 58: the country page's question on its relations with Russia, in the searchers' words ('Turkey Russia relations', 'Türkei Russland Beziehung', 'russia and south africa'), answered from its trade, support and net: in a language where the single-country queries of these clusters (seo_demand.json byLang) reach minDemand.

explain._note: Round 58: the explainers of seo_i18n.mjs EXPLAIN, shown where a topic page of seo_topics.json lists them (explain), and each also an FAQ entry (JSON-LD) in a language where the search demand of its keyword cluster (seo_demand.json _topics) reaches minDemand. An explainer without a cluster is never an FAQ entry.

armedItems._note: Round 58: the kinds of military supplies a country sent to Russia, in the searchers' words ('North Korea soldiers and shells', 'Iran drones'), named in titles, headings and questions only where the data have them: the country's weapons and troops sent to Russia come to at least minEur (EUR bn, full value) and src is one of the sources of its military_rus entry in data.json (the research that names those supplies). Their words in each language are in seo_i18n.mjs (S item).

research._note: Round 59b (owner approved: wire the three research results of round 59): fuel: what each country bought from Russia by fuel (fuel_split_r59.json), tables of the buyers of each fuel on the topic page named in topic (the rows first by customs, then by the map's basis), a section on the country pages where the five fuels on the map's basis come to at least country.minEur (EUR bn) and a war year's quality is one of country.quality, and the crude by year with the question on Russian oil where the customs of the last full year record at least crudeYears.minEur of crude and every war year's quality is one of crudeYears.quality; military: support for Ukraine by type (mil_split_r59.json), its page (slug) with the steps from Kiel's figure for the donors with a Kiel military figure of at least stepsMin (EUR bn), the share of GDP asked among economies of at least gdpMin, a section on the country pages and columns on the topic page named in support; deficit: Russia's federal budget balance and the National Wealth Fund (russia_deficit_r59.json), shown on the revenue page; revenue.balance names the research entry whose file has the budget's balance by year (yearly: balance_rub, balance_eur, balance_pct_gdp), from which the revenue page answers "What is Russia's budget deficit?". Each has a CSV in the downloads where it is a table of countries. Round 58b (owner approved): three research files the pages read at deploy (seo_research.mjs), in every language. sanctions: the sanctions on Russia that apply in each country and territory, a section and a question on every country page and the page of every country (slug); frozen: the amounts frozen in each holding country, on the country pages and as two columns of the topic page named in topic, and the totals in its explainers; revenue: Russia's federal oil and gas revenue, its page (slug), the months its monthly table shows, the topic page it links for the map's own measure (warIncome), and two CSV files in the downloads. check 48 reads every figure they write back against the file.
